newsitem.title: USA: US Chamber of Commerce to sue EPA on new air rules.
newsitem.headline: US Chamber of Commerce to sue EPA on new air rules.

text.p: The U.S. Chamber of Commerce said Thursday it planned to sue the Environmental Protection Agency over its new clean air standards because the agency failed to study the rules' impact on small businesses.
The EPA signed the controversial rules Wednesday, setting strict new limits on smog-forming ozone beginning in 2004 and on fine particles beginning in 2005.
Chamber officials said they were ready to file the lawsuit in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia circuit as soon as the rules are officially published in the next day or two.
"Anyone who thinks these regulations will strengthen the economy has been inhaling something stronger than ozone," said Robin Conrad, vice president of the U.S. Chamber's legal arm.
Under a law passed last year -- the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Act -- agencies are required to consider the impact their proposed rules might have on small business.

EPA Administrator Carol Browner has repeatedly said the rules are unlikely to hit small businesses because the most effective way to meet the new health standards would be to curb pollution from power plants and industrial plants.
The American Trucking Associations, the largest group representing the trucking industry, earlier announced that it planned to file a lawsuit challenging the regulations.

National Mining Association President Richard Lawson said Thursday that the coal industry also planned to sue the agency, but was first waiting to see whether Congress succeeded in overturning or delaying the new standards.
"For those parts that violate the law, we'll go to court," Lawson said at a conference sponsored by Energy Daily. "We'll stand by till we finish with the Congress."
